title: Finite labeled realization of a terminating maximum-center rule
statement:
Let $V$ be a totally ordered set with least element $ ot$, and fix a resolution invariant calculus $
u$ on all embedded rational pairs, including finite disjoint unions [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data]. Thus an initial pair $A=(X\hookrightarrow P)$ has $X$ reduced and $P$ smooth, separated and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. Consider admissible histories and maximum extensions [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. The following rule determines, up to the canonical isomorphisms of ordinary blowups, a finite history $T_
u(A)$ for every $A$: start with the empty history; stop if the current strict transform is regular; otherwise extend by the ordinary ambient blowup at the reduced full maximum locus of $
u$, taking scheme-theoretic strict transform. No exceptional-divisor cleanup is performed. This is a realization of the specified calculus, not an existence assertion for a calculus.

Write $m_i> ot$ for the maximum before its $i$th extension and label that extension by $m_i$ in the common ordered set $L=(V\setminus\{ ot\})^{\mathrm{op}}$. The active labels form a finite strictly increasing sequence in $L$. Every center is contained in the current strict transform, is nonempty, regular and nowhere dense there, with coherent ideals on the ambient and strict-transform schemes. All intermediate pairs are embedded rational pairs, and the last strict transform is regular. The history stops at its first regular stage. Empty and regular inputs have length zero. On a finite disjoint union, each extension uses the full maximum over the entire union in this same value set. For every lower cut of $L$, take the stage after exactly the active labels in that cut; this gives the finite labeled tower of [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution], with unit center ideal and identity transition at every inactive label. The realization retains all center ideals and their chronological order, including an ideal whose intrinsic blowup is an identity. No well-foundedness of $V$ is assumed.

source.place: ILO Expose VIII 2.3.1, 2.3.4--2.3.5 and 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.91--94; conditional history argument extracted from lem-trf-embedded-resolution-ambient-comparison, old Steps 1--2: realize the maximum-center recursion, terminate it, and index it by the reverse invariant order. BMT Theorem 6.1 Addendum and section 6.3 are the underlying detailed reference, archival copy WANTED; no Stacks tag states this conditional resolution-history lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-maximum-history-chronology] to the supplied calculus and pair. Its proved dependent-recursion argument gives a finite stopped chronology, positive reverse-order maximum labels, and all intermediate and center geometry.

Apply [lem-trf-maximum-history-lower-cut-tower] to that supplied chronology. Assemble its diagrams, cut index, initial identifications and retained center equations with the chronology fields to construct MaximumHistoryRealization, with no choice of a new history in a definition.

For any other realization with length s, forget labels and cuts in both realizations to obtain maximum segments. Apply [lem-trf-maximum-history-common-stage] at the shorter length. If r<s, regularity of the length-r endpoint transfers to the other segment at r, contradicting its nonregular source of the next extension. The case s<r is symmetric. Hence s=r and the existential length is unique.

The separate theorem maximumHistoryRealization_comparison remains to be proved. Its planned argument is unchanged: For completeness compare two choices of representatives in this recursion. Inductively identify their entire histories, beginning with the identity on $A$. This gives the smooth ambient comparison over the identity initial pair allowed by the history definition, with no deletions: every center is nonempty. The calculus smooth-value clause identifies their current functions, hence their greatest values and full maximum loci. Their reduced center ideals agree: on each affine open a reduced closed subscheme with support $Z$ has the radical ideal of $Z$. The ambient centers agree as well, by their closed immersions through $X_i$. The center ideal is coherent, hence of finite type, so its extended ideal on each of the two blowups is invertible [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]; for this same ideal the ordinary blowup universal property therefore gives inverse canonical comparison maps; the two composites are identities by uniqueness. The strict-transform definition identifies the next strict transforms, since an isomorphism carries the same open subscheme to the same scheme-theoretic closure. This extends the history identification and preserves all recorded ideals. The regularity test is invariant under these isomorphisms, so both histories stop at the same index. This proves the asserted determination up to canonical blowup identifications.
